title: Urban sprawl
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:41Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-suburbanisation-urban-sprawl, is written for Year 12 New South Wales and covers suburbanisation alongside sprawl, while the new point is a Year 7-8 Victorian point that defines sprawl and its three effects on farmland, travel and services, so the depth and scope differ enough that no bank point fits without a new card.

draft.title: Urban sprawl
card: Urban sprawl is when a city spreads outward into new suburbs. These suburbs are low-density, which means few homes on each hectare of land, mostly houses with yards.
Sprawl often grows over farmland and bush on the edge of a city. Land that was used for growing food or as habitat for plants and animals is built on.
People in outer suburbs often live far from jobs, schools and shops. Trips get longer, and many people rely on cars.

Homes are spread out, so there are fewer people in each area. This makes it harder and more costly to provide services such as water pipes and schools, and to run public transport that enough people use.
draft.remember: Sprawl spreads a city outward with low-density suburbs, which uses up land and makes travel and services harder.

a.q: Which description best fits urban sprawl?
opts: A city spreading outward in low-density suburbs
A city adding more flats in its centre
People moving from a city to a country town
A city planting more trees along its streets
a.why: Sprawl is outward growth into low-density suburbs on the city edge. Adding flats in the centre does the opposite, because it packs more people into the same area.
a.clue: Think about which direction the city is growing and how many homes fit on each hectare.

b.q: A new suburb of houses with large yards is built on farmland 40 km from the centre of a city. Few buses reach it. Which problem is most likely to result from this sprawl?
opts: Residents face long trips and rely on cars
Residents live too close to shops and jobs
Services are cheap to provide for so many people
Farmland near the city grows in area
b.why: The suburb is far from the centre and has low density, so trips are long and public transport is hard to provide. That leads to car use. The option about cheap services is wrong, because spread-out homes make services harder and more costly to supply.
b.clue: Think about how far people must travel and how many people live in each area.

a.best: A city spreading outward in low-density suburbs

b.best: Residents face long trips and rely on cars
